Frontend: /v/{unknown} renders public-video-error with 'This video is no longer available.' + err-cta and NO login redirect (verified from a fresh cookie-less session). /v/{valid_slug} renders public-video-page with video-title ('How Coffee Is Grown In Ethiopia'), creator-name ('Test User'), view-count ('118 views'), public-video-player pointing to /api/media/videos/demo.mp4, 3 storyboard tiles (public-scene-0/1/2), brand-link, topbar-signup, hero-cta-signup — both signup CTAs correctly navigate to /signup. ProjectView: when status=ready, share-btn is rendered next to download-btn/youtube-btn/instagram-btn; clicking opens share-modal containing share-url-input (with correct 10-char slug), share-copy-btn, share-revoke-btn, share-close-btn, and 4 socials (share-twitter/whatsapp/linkedin/email). Copy button writes exactly window.location.origin + '/v/' + slug to navigator.clipboard (verified by reading it back). Revoke button closes modal; reopening Share returns the SAME slug (idempotency guaranteed at UI level). Auth regression: newuser@test.com/secret123 still logs in successfully, dashboard reachable.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py has grown to 2561 lines. The >700-line-per-file guideline is now violated ~3.6x. Share endpoints (890-967), auth (400-620), projects, characters, TTS, schedulers, billing, waitlist, analytics all live in one file. Extraction into modules (routes/share.py, routes/auth.py, routes/projects.py, schedulers.py) is now materially overdue.

Public /api/public/videos/{slug} rate-limit uses IP-only bucketing (`_rate_limit_check(request, 'public_video', 120, 60)`). In shared-NAT / mobile-carrier / corporate-WiFi scenarios one popular share link could DoS every legitimate viewer behind the same egress IP after 120 req/min. Consider (slug + IP) or (creator_id + IP) composite key or raising limit for cached content — remember `share_view_count` is the growth-tracking metric, and hitting 429 silently degrades that.

public_video() ALWAYS looks up the creator via db.users.find_one on every hit — inefficient at scale. Cache creator_name into projects.creator_name at share-enable time (denormalize) so the hot public endpoint only touches ONE collection. Also avoids leaking timing signals about creator existence.

public_video() returns view_count = (share_view_count or 0) + 1 BEFORE awaiting the increment update — technically correct-looking to the client, but the $inc is `try:` fire-and-forget which swallows all errors. If Mongo is degraded, view_count silently drifts. Recommend awaiting the update_one and updating the response from the returned document, OR at minimum logging the exception.

share_slug uniqueness relies on find_one collision-check + insert without a transaction. Under high concurrent /share calls two workers could both see 'slug not taken' and race the update. The unique+sparse index will save data integrity (one insert 11000 will fail) but the current code path retries only 5x with NO try/except around update_one — a duplicate-key error would surface as a 500. Wrap the update in try/except DuplicateKeyError and re-loop.
video-title in PublicVideo.jsx uses `{data.title}` — if title is null (some legacy projects), the h1 renders empty. Fall back to topic or a friendly placeholder ('Untitled video by <creator>').

Public-video 404 message 'This video is no longer available.' is identical for (a) unknown slug and (b) disabled slug. Good for privacy (doesn't leak existence), but slightly bad for UX when a creator revokes their own link and re-shares the exact same URL — the recipient sees 'no longer available' with no way to distinguish. Consider an opt-in 'was revoked' hint via signed query param from the share modal (low priority).

Positive: private-field projection is correct (no user_id/email/password_hash/credits/role leaked at top-level OR in scene sub-objects). Only idx/heading/subtitle/image_url exposed per scene. Idempotency of POST /share is respected. DELETE /share correctly preserves share_slug so the same recipient bookmarks keep working after future re-enable. Unique+sparse index on projects.share_slug is present. Rate limit 120/min per IP triggers a clean 429 with 'Try again in 60s.' body.

rca of the issue: N/A — no bugs found. Two initial test failures during first parallel run were both test-side races: (1) test_public_projection_no_private_leak on worker gw0 fired GET /public/videos/{slug} at the exact moment worker gw1's test_disable_keeps_slug_reserved was calling DELETE /share — resulting in a transient 404. Fixed by prepending a POST /share re-enable inside the leak test. (2) A stale rate-limit bucket from the first parallel run pushed subsequent same-session tests over 120/min — resolved by `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` which flushed the in-memory bucket. All 11 tests then passed cleanly on the second run in 7.89s.
